newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand shares close at record high.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand shares close at record high.

text.p: The New Zealand share market surged to an all-time high on Monday as bullish sentiment -- quelled in recent weeks by a falling Kiwi dollar and rising interest rates -- reasserted itself.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index closed up 31.5 points, or 1.25 percent, at 2,542.11, with market leader Telecom rising 20 cents to NZ$7.85 and Tranzrail up 40 cents to $8.85.
It had set its previous high at 2,538 on July 5.
Brokers said some stocks were benefiting from the lower currency, which has fallen from 69 U.S. cents to 64.8 cents in less than six weeks, but the rally was broad-based and looked set to continue.

"I guess some companies are benefiting from a lower currency, but the market seems to have a much better tone about it, there's more interest in it and it's quite bullish," said Richard Burton at brokers Cavill White.
Tim Koller at Merrill Lynch said liquidity was a factor in the rally.

"I think it's got a lot to do with liquidity factors, there's just not a lot of supply of stock about," he said, adding that the Australian market's strength was also rubbing off on New Zealand shares.
Brokers said the positive sentiment was likely to remain in place unless the Dow had a sizeable correction overnight.
